changes.before: Create reminders with id as INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, title NOT NULL and nullable status DEFAULT open. Insert Read without a status and Walk with explicit NULL, with IDs 1 and 2.
changes.after: A default fills an omitted value; it does not replace an explicit NULL.

before: DEFAULT supplies a value when an INSERT does not provide that column. It is an insertion rule, not a query that keeps repairing missing data. A text literal uses single quotes. NULL represents missing information and is different from omitting a column.

The column list in INSERT INTO reminders(id,title) leaves status out, so its declared default is used. INSERT with all three values explicitly supplies NULL instead; this nullable column stores NULL. NOT NULL is a separate constraint: adding it would reject an explicit NULL with ordinary INSERT, rather than silently using the default. The project checks successful rows; the local error example below separately demonstrates the rejected write.
Optional practice: change the declared default to queued in a fresh database. Predict which of the two inserts changes.
after: `DEFAULT` supplies a starting value when an insert leaves out a column. It does not keep checking old rows or repair missing values later.
Leaving a column out is different from supplying `NULL`. An omitted column can use its default. An explicit NULL stays NULL when the column allows missing values.
The first insert leaves status out, so it uses the default. The second insert supplies a value—NULL—so the default is not used. A supplied text value would also take the place of the default.

`NOT NULL` is a separate rule that refuses missing values. The example requires a title but allows a missing status. With an ordinary INSERT, a default does not rescue an explicit NULL in a NOT NULL column.

Create `reminders` with an integer primary key `id`, a required text `title`, and a text `status` that allows NULL and defaults to `'open'`. Insert Read as id `1` without status. Insert Walk as id `2` with explicit NULL.

before.question: In a fresh table with status DEFAULT queued, insert one row without status and another with explicit NULL. What is stored?
before.explanation: Only the omitted column invokes its default. An explicit NULL remains NULL in a nullable column.

after.question: A status column allows NULL and defaults to queued. One insert omits status; another supplies NULL. What is stored?
after.explanation: Only the omitted value uses the default. The explicit NULL stays NULL.
